findings_for_runbook: F1 (blocking): the second receipt check MUST be defined against the check1-pinned receipt + checklist gates, NOT a re-run at the quarantine path. A re-run at qpath self-breaks for pushed (quarantine commit is unpushed by construction -> unpushed-commits-touching) and for moved-to-obsidian (rows cite the pre-mv path). It only passes for untracked stale artifacts (plain mv, no commit).

F2 (gate-opening, proven): bare origin + push + fetch + remote set-head converts NOT-SAFE(pushed-unverifiable) -> SAFE(pushed); works via origin/HEAD symref AND single-ref fallback. The live lane needs exactly this, operator-authorized, before any in-lane quarantine flow can pass even its first gate.

F3 (calibration divergence): the verdict engine awards SAFE(pushed) on a dirty worktree over the artifact (no dirty gate on the file-artifact branch). The SKILL decision table demands NOT-SAFE. Until reconciled, the quarantine flow MUST run the manual checklist dirty gate, not just the receipt re-run.
F4 (safe flow shape): untracked stale artifacts (plain mv, no quarantine commit) pass the entire flow including second check at qpath — the only fully green shape measured.

F5 (fixture/rig notes): ledger rows require canonical absolute source paths and SOUJI_LEDGER override off-lane; receipt order pushed->obsidian->stale means tracked+pushed scratch never reaches the stale receipt; symlink-present fires only in digest scopes.

summary.verdict: Operability proven on fixtures; 3 flow-design/calibration findings banked for the runbook (F1 second-check definition, F2 gate-opening steps, F3 dirty divergence). All three installed tools green; zero live mutations; no authorized live targets (receipts deny, S9).
